title: Agedashi Tofu Crispy Dashi

description: Experience the delightful contrast of crispy fried tofu exterior and silken interior, bathed in a warm, savory dashi broth. This classic Japanese vegetarian dish, Agedashi Tofu, offers a comforting and elegant appetizer or light meal. Garnished with fresh ingredients, it's a symphony of textures and umami flavors perfect for any occasion.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tofu
instructions.text: Press the tofu block to remove excess water. Wrap it in paper towels or a clean kitchen towel and place a heavy object on top for at least 15-20 minutes. Once pressed, cut the tofu into 8-12 uniform cubes, about 1.5-inch pieces.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dashi Broth
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine the vegetarian kombu dashi broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar (if using). Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low to keep it warm. Do not boil vigorously to preserve the delicate dashi flavor.

instructions.title: Coat the Tofu
instructions.text: Place the potato starch in a shallow dish. Gently dredge each tofu cube in the starch, ensuring it is evenly coated on all sides. Lightly shake off any excess starch. This coating is crucial for achieving a crispy exterior.

instructions.title: Fry the Tofu
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot or wok to 350-360F (175-180C). Carefully add the coated tofu cubes to the hot oil in batches to avoid overcrowding. Fry for 3-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Use a slotted spoon to remove the tofu and place it on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.

instructions.title: Assemble the Dish
instructions.text: Arrange the crispy fried tofu cubes in individual serving bowls. Pour the warm dashi broth generously over the tofu, allowing it to soak slightly. The tofu will absorb the broth, becoming flavorful while retaining some crispness.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Garnish each bowl with a mound of grated daikon radish, a small amount of grated fresh ginger, and a sprinkle of sliced green onions. For a touch of spice, add a pinch of shichimi togarashi. Serve immediately while the tofu is warm and crispy.

tips: Ensure your tofu is well-pressed; removing excess water is key to achieving a crispy exterior and preventing oil splatters during frying.
For the crispiest result, maintain a consistent oil temperature around 350-360F (175-180C). Frying in batches helps prevent the oil temperature from dropping too much.
Serve Agedashi Tofu immediately after assembly. While the dashi broth will soften the coating over time, the initial crispness and warmth are part of its unique charm.
